module_title: Joinder of Charges, Section 351 BNSS, and Marshalling Evidence
introduction: This intermediate tier drives into the exceptions allowing multiple crimes to be tried together (Joinder of Charges), the crucial stage where the judge questions the accused directly, and how a judge marshals criminal evidence to write a bulletproof conviction.

core_concepts.title: Exceptions to Separate Trials (Joinder of Charges)
core_concepts.description:
While Section 241 BNSS mandates separate charges for distinct offenses, Sections 242-246 provide exceptions to avoid multiple trials:
1. Same kind of offense (Sec 242): Up to 3 offenses of the same kind committed within one year can be tried together.
2. Same Transaction (Sec 243): If a series of acts are so connected together as to form the 'same transaction', they can be tried together (e.g., A breaks into a house, steals a TV, and shoots the guard escaping. House-trespass, theft, and assault are tried together).

core_concepts.title: Alteration of Charge (Section 239, BNSS)
core_concepts.description:
Can a judge change a charge midway through a trial?
- The Rule: Any Court may alter or add to any charge at any time **before judgment is pronounced**.
- Safeguard: Every such alteration or addition MUST be read and explained to the accused. If the alteration prejudices the accused's defense, the court must adjourn the trial or direct a new trial.

core_concepts.title: Power to Examine the Accused (Section 351, BNSS)
core_concepts.description:
Formerly Section 313 CrPC. This is a vital part of a criminal judgment.
- The Rule: After the prosecution witnesses are examined, the judge MUST question the accused generally on the case to give them an opportunity to personally explain any incriminating circumstances appearing in the evidence.
- Application in Judgment: A judge must write down what the accused said in this statement. The accused cannot be punished for giving false answers here, but false answers can be used to draw adverse inferences.

core_concepts.title: Marshalling & Appreciation of Evidence
core_concepts.description:
A criminal judge must weave the evidence systematically under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA), 2023.
- Falsus in uno, falsus in omnibus: 'False in one thing, false in everything'. This Latin maxim is **NOT applied in India**. Just because a witness lied about one detail does not mean their entire testimony is thrown out. The judge's duty is to separate the 'grain from the chaff' (truth from falsehood).

important_entities.name: Hostile Witness
important_entities.key_fact: A witness who turns against the party who called them.
important_entities.significance: Under the BSA, if a prosecution witness turns hostile (changes their statement to favor the accused), their testimony is not automatically washed off the record. The judge can still rely on the part of their testimony that aligns with the prosecution's case, if it is corroborated.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Advanced exams test exceptions to the burden of proof. Normally, the prosecution must prove guilt. However, if the accused claims a General Exception under the BNS (e.g., 'I was insane at the time' or 'I acted in self-defense'), the burden to prove that exception lies strictly on the **accused** (Section 108, BSA).

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: The two most common reasons a judge will merge multiple crimes into a single trial to save judicial time.

exam_strategy_tips: In your Judgment Writing paper, always dedicate a specific paragraph detailing how you evaluated the 'Statement of the Accused under Section 351 BNSS' before reaching your final conclusion.
